Database, pooler and store hops are in tls-data-tier; the full per-hop list is the §12.1 table in docs/secrets/cert-manager.md. local-stack is plaintext by design and is not drawn.

div.div:
Reading the hop state
TLS verified: the client checks the chain against a CA and checks the hostname. TLS unverified: the hop is encrypted, but the client does not check who answers. PLAINTEXT: nothing is encrypted on the hop. Behind the edge every request, identity and east-west hop is plaintext: Envoy has no BackendTLSPolicy, Keycloak serves HTTP in-cluster, gRPC between services uses insecure credentials, and OpenBao runs tls_disable. Only the two OIDC hairpins (OpenBao, Flux web UI) verify, against the live homelab-ca. Operator-managed TLS (OpenBao Raft cluster port, Envoy Gateway xDS, chart webhook Issuers) uses each operator's own CA. kubelet and kube-apiserver scrapes use TLS with insecureSkipVerify.

div.div:
Planned, not installed (RFC-0020, provisional)
S0 edge issuer decouple · S1 OpenBao listener TLS · S6 gRPC + Temporal mTLS · S7 intermediate CA · S8 Keycloak HTTPS · S10 Envoy BackendTLSPolicy · S13 OCI registry TLS + cosign · S14 KMS over HTTPS (production). S2–S4 shipped through ADR-089 and are drawn in tls-data-tier.
